paper.note: SAME UNDERLYING PAPER as mg34 doc 226481 — the 2026/27 Treasury Strategy Appendix B2 that went first to the Governance and Audit Committee on 9 February 2026 and was then recommended on to Council on 26 February 2026. Content is identical (independent read confirms every table foots the same way). This mg35 read adds ONE thing the mg34 read did not have: the Capital Strategy Appendix A (doc 227026) is tabled at the Council pack and prints the weighted rate on the PWLB book (5.01% on £167.5m) that Appendix B2 itself omits. That is the rate-quote cross-check the mg34 note flagged as unavailable. Two other companion papers held from the same 26 February Council meeting: doc 227025 (5pp covering report) and doc 227023 (MRP Policy) with its Appendix A (doc 227024). All papers on disk; nothing fetched from the council website.

facts.value: Total borrowing £212,022,508 at 8 January 2026 — PWLB £167,522,508, other local authorities £34,500,000, market (banking-sector) £10,000,000, all fixed-rate. Investments: £42,000,000, all short-term. 25% market-loan cap policy — currently at 4.72%.
facts.note: Table 1 (Appendix B2 p.2) sums 167,522,508 + 34,500,000 + 10,000,000 = 212,022,508 exactly. Ties to £212.0m external borrowing at 31 December 2025 quoted in the Q3 25/26 covering report (mg34 doc 226476 §3.5, held on disk). The weighted rates on each tranche are NOT in Appendix B2 itself — they are in the Capital Strategy Appendix A (doc 227026, treasury management section): PWLB 5.01%, Market 4.92%, other LAs 4.44%, investments 3.86%.

facts.value: PWLB £167.5m at weighted 5.01% at 8 January 2026 (per doc 227026, Capital Strategy Appendix A, treasury management section). Our bc-loans file for CONWY COUNTY BOROUGH COUNCIL holds 50 loans at £172,674,509 at weighted 5.0019% as at 2026-03-31, with 49 live loans totalling £161,062,700 today (2026-08-15). Rate ties to <0.1bp; principal off by £5.15m (3.1%).
facts.note: The RATE tie (5.0019% vs 5.01%) is a clean cross-check the mg34 note did not have — Appendix B2 itself prints no weighted rate on the PWLB book. Principal difference sits on our side: bc-loans `--as-at 2026-01-08` mode returns only 18 loans / £85.9m, impossible against the paper's own £167.5m, so the Start-date limitation flagged in EMAIL_TEMPLATE.md §7 applies here. The maturity-profile bucket sum on today's 49 live loans (7,200,000 + 3,980,430 + 5,854,745 + 64,188,995 + 18,709,620 + 67,740,718) = £167,674,508 — that lines up with £167,522,508 to within £152k, so the current live book essentially matches the paper's 8 January position to <0.1%. Table 7's own trajectory has debt FALLING £7.1m across 2025/26, so our £172.674m at 31 March 2026 being higher than the paper's £167.523m at 8 January cannot both be right — the file overstates the year-end position.

facts.value: Loans CFR grows from £234.188m at 31.3.25 (actual) to £253.167m (31.3.26 est), £282.603m (31.3.27), £290.249m (31.3.28) and £291.933m (31.3.29) — a £57.745m increase across the strategy period. Gross CFR peaks at £335.748m in 31.3.28. OLTL declines from £54.302m to £41.892m as PFI and leases run off.
facts.note: Table 6 foots exactly year by year: Gross CFR less OLTL = Loans CFR. Movement in loans CFR = financing need less MRP/VRP and other movements, foots exactly.

facts.value: Over-borrowed by £2.898m at 31.3.25 actual; becomes under-borrowed by £23.181m at 31.3.26 estimate — a £26.079m swing to an internally-borrowed position inside a single year. Held broadly at that level: −£22.723m (26/27), −£21.727m (27/28), −£20.811m (28/29).
facts.note: Table 7 arithmetic ties to Table 6 exactly (see reconciliation). External borrowing fell £19.5m April to December 2025 per mg34 doc 226476 §3.5. Page 4 of the strategy states the choice explicitly: with short-term rates higher and rates expected to fall, 'it is therefore likely to be more cost effective over the medium-term to either use internal resources, or to borrow short-term and medium-term loans instead including PWLB loans.'

facts.value: Rises from £206.161m at 31.3.25 to £225.167m (31.3.26 est), £254.603m (31.3.27), £262.249m (31.3.28) and £263.933m (31.3.29). Balance-sheet resources held flat at £38.000m; liquidity allowance £10.000m throughout.
facts.note: Table 4's Loans CFR row matches Table 6 exactly. Arlingclose LB chart on page 7 shows existing fixed-rate loans falling from c.£200m in 2024 to c.£80m by 2032, then continuing to decline; loans CFR peaks around 2028 at c.£280m before drifting down. The gap between Loans CFR and existing fixed-rate loans on the chart is the future new-borrowing requirement — visible into the 2050s.

facts.value: 5.81% (24/25 actual), 5.66% (25/26 forecast), 6.10% (26/27 budget), 6.38% (27/28 forecast), 6.30% (28/29 forecast). Absolute financing costs £17.093m → £22.702m over five years, a £5.609m rise.
facts.note: 72 bps of ratio headroom consumed between 25/26 forecast and 27/28 forecast peak; eases 8 bps in 28/29. CRMP funding held flat at −£2.632m from 25/26 onwards. PFI/Coed Pella financing runs down from £3.745m to £2.813m.

LIMITS only. The paper does not print the actual bucket percentages of Conwy's own book. Q3 compliance is asserted at doc 227025 §12.1 by the G&A Committee on 9 February 2026; underlying figures sit in the Q3 report Appendix (mg34 doc 226476 Appendix A) which is not on disk.

facts.value: Bank Rate cut to 3.75% in December (p.3 verbatim). Arlingclose expects Bank Rate to be cut to 3.25% by middle of 2026, with near-term upside risks. Central-case 10-year gilt: 4.52% current → 4.30% by mid-2026. 20-year: 5.16% → 4.90%. 50-year: 4.74% → 4.60%.
facts.note: Testable forecast. Bank Rate today (2026-08-14 market snapshot) is 3.75% — the December cut held but the forecast further cut to 3.25% has not materialised. PWLB 10-year certainty today is 5.83% (notice 314/26 PM); against a certainty margin of 80bps over gilts that implies a 10-year gilt around 5.0-5.1% — roughly 70-80bps higher than Arlingclose's mid-2026 forecast of 4.30%.

facts.value: External borrowing decreased £19.5m (from £231.5m to £212.0m) during April to December 2025. Investments decreased £13.2m (from £40.6m to £27.4m) over the same period. Full compliance with prudential indicators asserted (Q3).
facts.note: The Q3 25/26 covering report was tabled at the earlier G&A Committee (mg34) and does not appear in the 26 February Council pack, but its narrative is background for the strategy's 8 January 2026 position. The detailed Q3 appendix lives in Appendix A of that item and is not held. The £212.0m at 31 December ties exactly to Table 1's £212,022,508 at 8 January 2026 in the strategy paper.

Full programme running total at 20 January 2026 is £117.070m (£66.693m in 2025/26, £50.377m in later years). Revenue and capital budgets 2026/27 to Council on 5 March 2026 (doc 227025 §3.1).

reconciliation.balance_sheet_identity: Applied year by year. Loans CFR (Table 6) minus external borrowing (Table 7: opening + expected change) equals internal borrowing. 31.3.25 actual: 234,188 − 237,086 = −2,898 (over-borrowed £2.9m); Table 7 prints +2,898 — EXACT. 31.3.26 est: 253,167 − 229,986 = +23,181 (internal); Table 7 prints (23,181) — EXACT. 31.3.27: 282,603 − 259,880 = +22,723; Table 7 prints (22,723) — EXACT. 31.3.28: 290,249 − 268,521 = +21,728; Table 7 prints (21,727) — off by £1k (rounding). 31.3.29: 291,933 − 271,122 = +20,811; Table 7 prints (20,811) — EXACT. Identity closes across all five years.
reconciliation.loan_book_tie: RATE TIES to <0.1bp: our bc-loans file for CONWY COUNTY BOROUGH COUNCIL at 2026-03-31 shows 50 loans at weighted 5.0019%; doc 227026 (Capital Strategy Appendix A) states the PWLB book at 8 January 2026 is 'at an average interest rate of 5.01%'. Principal DOES NOT TIE cleanly: our £172,674,509 at 31.3.26 vs the paper's £167,522,508 at 8.1.26 — a £5.15m gap (3.1%). Table 7's own trajectory has debt falling £7.1m across 2025/26, so our end-year figure being higher than their part-year figure is not consistent with the paper's own direction of travel; the gap sits on our side (Start-date limitation in bc-loans, flagged EMAIL_TEMPLATE.md §7). Interestingly, our maturity-profile bucket sum at 2026-08-15 (£167,674,508 across 49 live loans) essentially matches the paper's 8.1.26 figure of £167,522,508 to £152k (<0.1%), which further supports the view that our snapshot at 2026-03-31 overstates. Disclose the loan-count/principal on our side, quote the 5.01% rate tie confidently, do not invite the council to correct us.
reconciliation.table_sums: Table 1: 167.523 + 34.500 + 10.000 = 212.023 exact. Table 4 net loans requirement + liquidity allowance = liability benchmark each year — exact. Table 5 total expenditure less capital receipts + grants + reserves = net financing need each year — exact. Table 6 movement in loans CFR = financing need less MRP/VRP — exact. Table 7 estimated gross debt at 31 March = prior year opening + change (both for debt and OLTL) — exact. Table 8 authorised limit total = borrowing + OLTL each year — exact.
reconciliation.rates_check: The RATE tie 5.0019% (bc-loans, 31.3.26) vs 5.01% (doc 227026 Appendix A, 8.1.26) is the credible cross-check for the loan-book reconciliation. The paper does not print a prevailing PWLB certainty rate at 8 January 2026; the Arlingclose gilt forecast (page 4) is not directly comparable to PWLB certainty rates.

summary.text:
Cyngor Conwy's 2026/27 Treasury Strategy was received by Council on 26 February 2026, having been recommended by Governance and Audit Committee on 9 February. The paper is the same document already read as mg34 doc 226481. This mg35 read confirms every table foots the same way and, importantly, adds a piece the mg34 read did not have: the Capital Strategy Appendix A tabled at the Council pack (doc 227026) prints the weighted rate on Conwy's PWLB book at 5.01% — a figure the Treasury Strategy Appendix B2 itself omits and that closes the rate-quote gap flagged in mg34's own reconciliation.

The story of the paper is a £26m swing to internal borrowing in a single year. Table 7 has Conwy over-borrowed by £2.9m at 31 March 2025 actual and under-borrowed by £23.2m at 31 March 2026 estimate, then holding broadly at that level through 2028/29 (−£22.7m, −£21.7m, −£20.8m). The Q3 covering (mg34 doc 226476) confirms the mechanism: external borrowing fell £19.5m April to December 2025, from £231.5m to £212.0m, and investments came down £13.2m alongside. Page 4 of the strategy states the choice explicitly — with short rates higher than long rates and rates expected to fall, internal or short-medium borrowing is 'more cost effective over the medium-term'. That is a real, testable decision, and rarer in the strategies we read than it ought to be.

The forward pressure is real too. Loans CFR grows £57.7m across the strategy period (£234.2m at 31.3.25 to £291.9m at 31.3.29), while OLTL runs off £54.3m to £41.9m as PFI and leases mature. Table 9 shows financing costs rising from £17.1m (24/25 actual) to a peak of £22.3m in 27/28, and the ratio to net revenue stream climbing from 5.66% (25/26 forecast) to 6.38% (27/28 forecast) — 72 bps of headroom consumed at the peak, then easing 8 bps in 28/29. The liability benchmark (Table 4) climbs from £206m (31.3.25) to £264m (31.3.29); the Arlingclose LB chart on page 7 shows the existing fixed-rate book running off from c.£200m today to c.£80m by 2032 — the gap is the new borrowing decision the strategy centres on.

Our loan-book reconciliation ties on rate to less than 0.1 basis point (5.0019% on our bc-loans file for CONWY COUNTY BOROUGH COUNCIL at 31.3.26 against the paper's 5.01% at 8.1.26) and to £152k on the maturity-bucket sum at today's date (£167,674,508 across 49 live loans against the paper's £167,522,508). The 31.3.26 principal in our file (£172,674,509 across 50 loans) is £5.15m above the paper's 8.1.26 £167,522,508 — but Table 7's own trajectory has debt FALLING £7.1m across 2025/26, so the direction is on the paper's side, not ours; the Start-date limitation in bc-loans (EMAIL_TEMPLATE.md §7) explains why our as-at snapshots run high. Balance-sheet arithmetic ties exactly across all five years of Table 7 to £1k of rounding. Adviser: Arlingclose Ltd. Officers named: Gareth Evans (Head of Finance), Huw Ifor Jones (Principal Accountant), Cllr Chris Cater (Cabinet Member for Finance) — no email address for any of them printed anywhere in the pack, no s151 title identified.

officer.body:
Hi [OFFICER FIRST NAME],

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's premature repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the SONIA path, the rate predictor, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. So below are a few thoughts on the 2026/27 Treasury Strategy that went to Council on 26 February, after Governance and Audit on 9 February. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it.

One cross-check first. Your Capital Strategy Appendix A reports the PWLB book at £167.5m at 8 January 2026 at an average interest rate of 5.01%. Our loan file for you holds the same 50 PWLB loans at a weighted 5.0019% — a tie to less than a tenth of a basis point on the rate, and to within £152k on the current bucket sum against your Table 1 figure. On the count and total principal we're carrying £172.7m as at 31 March 2026 in our file, £5.2m above your 8 January figure — that gap sits on our side (our file has some known unreliability on drawdown-date fields, and your Table 7 shows external borrowing FALLING £7.1m across 2025/26, so the direction is with your figure not ours). Flagging it so you know the number we're working from, not to ask you to correct us.

The headline in your paper is a £26m move. Table 7 has Conwy over-borrowed by £2.9m at 31 March 2025 and under-borrowed by £23.2m at 31 March 2026 estimated — a £26.1m swing to an internally-borrowed position inside a single year, held broadly at that level (−£22.7m, −£21.7m, −£20.8m) through 2028/29. The Q3 covering makes the mechanism clean: external borrowing dropped £19.5m between April and December 2025, from £231.5m to £212.0m. Your page 4 explains the choice plainly — with short-term rates higher than long rates and rates expected to fall, internal or short-medium borrowing is more cost-effective over the medium term. That is a real decision, and rarer in the strategies we read than it should be.

The cost-of-carry maths behind the choice is where the market has an opinion. When your paper was written Arlingclose expected Bank Rate to be cut to 3.25% by the middle of 2026; today, six months on, Bank Rate is still 3.75% — the December cut held but the next one hasn't come. The Arlingclose 10-year gilt central case for later 2026 was 4.30%; PWLB 10-year certainty closed yesterday afternoon at 5.83% on notice 314/26, implying the underlying gilt is around 5.0% — roughly 70 basis points higher than the forecast. Your existing external book is insulated because it's already drawn and 100% fixed. What's exposed is the £38.8m of Loans CFR growth planned across the strategy period (£253m at 31 March 2026 rising to £292m by 31 March 2029, from Table 6), because that block has to be funded either from cash (extending the £23m internal position) or from new external borrowing at today's curve rather than the one Arlingclose was forecasting. Your Table 9 already prices some of this in — financing costs to net revenue stream go from 5.66% to 6.38% at the 27/28 peak — but the shape of the funding decision within it is a live one.

Where we might be useful is the tool the CIPFA Prudential and Treasury Code updates put at the centre — the liability benchmark. Your Table 4 climbs from £206m at 31 March 2025 to £264m at 31 March 2029, and the Arlingclose chart on page 7 shows the existing fixed-rate book running off from around £200m today to £80m by 2032. The gap between those two lines is the future new-borrowing requirement, and it's the shape most sensitive to the timing question the strategy raises. We publish live curves underneath the benchmark so the point where the two lines meet — and the notional cost of closing them — move with the market rather than being recalculated once a year. Yours is at pwlbtoday.org/loan-analysis.

For the market itself: PWLB certainty on 14 August was 4.95% at one year, 5.34% at five, 5.83% at ten, 6.38% at twenty, 6.46% at twenty-five and 6.27% at fifty. That breakdown, alongside the monthly sector activity, is at pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity.

One smaller observation, for context rather than action. Your PWLB book prices about £0.75m below par on the DMO's premature repayment curve today — a net discount of 0.5% of principal, with 12 of the 49 live loans below par and the largest single discount on the 2067 maturity at 2.30%. Nothing follows from that: we don't sell treasury products, we model no MRP or accounting treatment, only the DMO can quote, and whether anything would be worth doing turns on replacement cost we do not model. It's just where the book sits on today's curve, priced daily.
